item.title: Tai Po fire timeline: Wang Fuk Court’s HK$330 million renovation, ignored warnings and aftermath
item.description: The fire that broke out at Tai Po’s Wang Fuk Court on November 26 has become Hong Kong’s deadliest blaze in almost eight decades – but it may have been long in the making. item.title: HKFP Lens: Spectacular bamboo theatre centrepiece of Kam Tin’s centuries-old Jiao Festival
item.description: Kam Tin’s spectacular week-long, once-in-a-decade thanksgiving festival continues until Friday. The centrepiece of the centuries-old Jiao festival is an illuminated HK$20 million bamboo, tin roof theatre, surrounded by flags. The Kam Tin tradition dates back to 1685. Taiping Qingjiao ceremonies are held to request blessings from Taoist deities for a particular location or neighbourhood. The […]

item.title: Hong Kong director says film was denied public screening on national security grounds
item.description: A Hong Kong director has said his latest film has been denied a public screening in the city by authorities on the grounds that it could harm national security. item.title: Teenager jailed for 3.5 years over Hong Kong independence group involvement
item.description: A 16-year-old boy has been sentenced to three and a half years in prison for conspiring to commit secession by “actively participating” in a Taiwan-based group that advocates Hong Kong independence. The defendant, whose name was not disclosed as he is a minor, faced sentencing at the District Court on Monday. He had earlier pleaded […]

item.title: Hong Kong man pleads guilty to damaging election posters, says he tore off only fingertip-sized piece
item.description: A Hong Kong man has pleaded guilty to one count of criminal damage after being accused of vandalising election posters, saying that he had only torn off a piece of a poster the size of his fingertip. item.title: China to impose anti-dumping duties on EU pork for 5 years
item.description: China will impose anti-dumping duties on European Union pork imports for five years, but at lower rates than temporary levies in place since September, Beijing announced Tuesday. The two economic powerhouses have been locked in a trade spat fuelled by what many European countries view as an unbalanced economic relationship with China. The levies come […]

item.description: The storming of the Legislative Council (LegCo) in 2019 was “unprecedented,” a Hong Kong prosecutor has argued after seven people sentenced for rioting in the complex appealed for lighter jail terms. item.title: Hong Kong cancels New Year’s Eve fireworks; alternative countdown event to convey ‘positive energy’
item.description: The Hong Kong government has called off the New Year’s Eve fireworks display following the deadly Tai Po fire, replacing it with an alternative countdown event aimed at conveying “positive energy.” The government said in a press release on Wednesday night that this year’s countdown will “forgo” the fireworks display. item.title: Washington approves US$11 billion in arms sales to Taiwan: Taipei
item.description: Washington has approved $11 billion-worth of arms to Taiwan, Taipei said Thursday, announcing one of the largest weapons packages for the island as it seeks to deter a potential Chinese invasion.
